rule: One integer timer per status (player or monster). The status word shown is the grade the timer sits in; grades are turn thresholds. Player increases add to the timer and are blocked only by NONSTACKING (paralysis). Monster effects use one of three stack rules per effect: NO, MAX or INCR. Stun-on-hit amounts are rolled by critical tier, then the grade ladder decides the word and the penalty. Monster resist is a level-based roll (cap 90 percent) with a double roll for uniques, and certain monster flags auto-resist. Cut damage per turn scales with grade (1, 2 or 3). Stun gives a to-hit and damage penalty by grade, and Knocked Out removes the turn.
keep: One word per grade on the status line, with the grade name carrying the danger
Grade thresholds as data, not code
NONSTACKING flag for hard disables (no re-paralyse while held)
Monster resist roll tied to monster level, with a unique double check
Minimum turns floor on a new monster effect (2 turns)
Stun as a short miss chance and a damage and accuracy cut, not a full lock
change: Seven cut grades is too many for a 375 phone; use three or four
Do not roll a new random tier per hit on top of a critical roll; one server roll per hit
Names, message strings and numbers are ours, not the donor's
Stun with three attackers: use MAX not INCR, so stacked stuns do not add into a long lock
Fear per attacker needs a cap; the donor fear is INCR, which we should bound
look_test: On the existing duel scene: one enemy's hit gives a bleed that moves from its first word to its second after two hits; a second enemy's hit gives a stun that moves Stun to Heavy Stun. Show the word chip above the health bar at 375 wide. Compare the grade-word chip against an icon with a number. Dom judges whether the danger is readable at a glance without a number.
